questions.a: B) Matt black. Dark matt surfaces are the best emitters and absorbers.

questions.q: Efficiency of a lamp: 20 J light from 100 J?
Name the energy store in food.
Hot air rises because it is...
Efficiency can never be more than...
Big question: why does a vacuum flask keep tea hot for hours?
questions.a: The vacuum stops conduction and convection and the silvered walls reduce radiation.

questions.q: A TV uses 120 J; 30 J is light and sound. Efficiency?
questions.model: Useful output: 30 J. Total: 120 J. Efficiency = 30 ÷ 120 × 100 = 25%.

questions.q: Explain why radiators are near the floor.
questions.a: Air near the radiator warms, becomes less dense and rises (1), setting up a convection current that heats the room (1).

questions.q: Why do pans have copper bases?
questions.a: Copper is a good thermal conductor.

questions.q: Explain how a vacuum flask reduces energy transfer by conduction, convection and radiation. Portal response box.
questions.a: Vacuum: no particles, so no conduction (1) or convection (1) across the gap; silvered walls reflect infrared (1), reducing radiation (1); stopper reduces convection and evaporation from the top (1); plastic is an insulator (1).
questions.model: Teacher writes the first point: 'The vacuum between the walls has no particles, so energy cannot be transferred across it by conduction.'

questions.q: Describe an experiment to compare the infrared emitted by different surfaces (Leslie cube or cans of hot water).
questions.a: Cans painted different colours, same volume of hot water (1); measure temperature drop over the same time (1); fastest cooling is the best emitter (matt black) (1).

questions.q: A device is 40% efficient and wastes 300 J. What was the total input?
questions.a: Wasted energy is 60% of the input (1); input = 300 ÷ 0.6 = 500 J (1)
